bias.headline: Conditions are clearly bearish (led by Risk Appetite). This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBearish.label: Risk Appetite
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 2nd percentile.
topBearish.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 4.7% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 2% of them

topBearish.label: Volatility
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBearish.explanation: SPY typically moves 1.49% in a day right now — more volatile than 85% of its own past. That is elevated volatility, and stocks tend to get more violent on the way down than on the way up.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 85% of them

topBearish.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing high rejected; no reclaim above 772.31
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 12 swing highs and 11 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 9% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
topBearish.explanation: SPY is printing lower highs and lower lows — an intact downtrend. Last swing high 766.81 vs prior 772.31; last swing low 759.97 vs prior 763.25.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
topBearish.nextTrigger: breaks up above the last swing high of 766.81

watchNext.label: Market Breadth
watchNext.confidenceBasis: 95 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
watchNext.explanation: 56% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is about typical — higher than 46% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 57%.
watchNext.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
conflicts: Participation is ordinary for this panel — neither unusually broad nor unusually narrow.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only picks a side once it reaches the top or bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 46% of them, which is the middle

watchNext.label: Trend Strength
watchNext.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.07 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
watchNext.explanation: Over 60 sessions SPY moved -2.8%, and only 7% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
watchNext.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.07 now

metrics.explanation: 56% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is about typical — higher than 46% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 57%.
metrics.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
conflicts: Participation is ordinary for this panel — neither unusually broad nor unusually narrow.
metrics.nextTrigger: only picks a side once it reaches the top or bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 46% of them, which is the middle

metrics.label: Trend Strength
metrics.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.16 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions IWM moved -7.2%, and only 16% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
metrics.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is negative but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.16 now

metrics.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing low held; no structural break below 270.44
metrics.confidenceBasis: 13 swing highs and 9 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 13% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
metrics.explanation: IWM is printing higher highs and higher lows — an intact uptrend. Last swing high 284.02 vs prior 284.01; last swing low 275.75 vs prior 270.44.
metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
metrics.nextTrigger: breaks down below the last swing low of 275.75

categories.label: Money Flow
categories.topReason: Risk Appetite: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 4.7% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.

metrics.label: Risk Appetite
metrics.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 2nd percentile.
metrics.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 4.7% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
metrics.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 2% of them

categories.label: Risk & Volatility
categories.topReason: Volatility: IWM typically moves 1.79% in a day right now — more volatile than 61% of its own past. That is unremarkable for this name.

metrics.label: Volatility
metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
metrics.explanation: IWM typically moves 1.79% in a day right now — more volatile than 61% of its own past. That is unremarkable for this name.
metrics.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
metrics.nextTrigger: only picks a side once it reaches the top or bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 61% of them, which is the middle
